message:
Goal: apply your 5 PM notes to the proto-clinic prototype, leave the Invoices screen untouched, and commit the result.

**Found:**
- Prototype: `proto-clinic/index.html`, plain HTML with four screens (Today, Clients, Invoices, Settings). It is the only one in the folder.
- Notes: your message. There is no `CLAUDE.md` and no reference to copy.
- Invoices is off limits (note 3), so its text and looks are compared before and after, and the shared table and pill styles stay as they are.
- The folder is not a git repository and has no remote, so "commit and push to main" cannot run as written (question 2).
- Already broken, left alone: the "New appointment" button does nothing, and the Invoices Overdue filter shows an empty table.

**Track:** full (no reference, so both tracks are the same).
**Coverage:** 6 clear · partial: Edge cases, Words with no number · missing: Outputs (git)

**Done means:**
- Settings has no description paragraph under any heading
- Today table has a Status column; every row says arrived, waiting or in session
- Save changes on Settings shows a toast and no grey "Saved"
- Invoices screen is identical before and after
- A local link opens the prototype

**Your notes as I read them:**
- R1 everywhere: remove the description under headings (my reading: the lorem paragraph under "Booking policy")
- R2 Today: add a "Status" column, one pill per row (my reading: sample values, display only)
- R3 Settings: toast "Settings saved" at the bottom right, gone after 3 s, replaces the grey "Saved" (my reading)
- R4 commit when done, push to main (blocked, see question 2)

About 30 minutes and 2 helper agents, within a budget of 60 minutes.

**Questions**

1. Note 1 says "descriptions under every heading". The only grey description text I find is the lorem paragraph under "Booking policy" on Settings (that label is not a heading). Should the small captions under the Today numbers ("appointments", "therapists in", "unpaid this week") go too?
   Recommended: no. Remove only the Booking policy paragraph, and keep the stat captions.
   Why it matters: removing the captions makes the three Today cards bare numbers with no meaning.

2. This folder is not a git repository and has no remote, so there is nothing to push to. What should I do?
   Recommended: run `git init` and make one local commit of the change. Do not push, and name the one command you run once you add a remote.
   Why it matters: a push to a remote I invent could publish to the wrong place, and without a repo nothing can be committed.

3. Which sample status goes on which Today row?
   Recommended: Priya Nair in session, Owen Brooks arrived, Mei Chen waiting, Luis Ortega and Hannah Weiss waiting.
   Why it matters: the values are made-up data, and you may want them to tell a specific story in a demo.

Notes sent later still join this run. Everything else (the full needs table, the coverage table) goes in `brief.md` once you reply.

Reply with your answers, or just "go" to use the defaults.

evidence.completeness: All five topics settled: descriptions (Q1), Status column (R2/Q3), Invoices "identical before and after", toast "Settings saved... gone after 3 s", commit/push blocked with Q2.
evidence.no_redundancy: States the prototype and the Invoices lock as found facts ("It is the only one in the folder", "Invoices is off limits (note 3)") rather than asking; Q3 on sample row values is low-stakes but not answerable from files.
evidence.defaults_quality: Every question has a concrete default: "Remove only the Booking policy paragraph", "run git init and make one local commit... Do not push", a named status per row.
evidence.clarity: Three ordered questions with reasons, but the brief carries jargon and clutter ("Track: full", "Coverage: 6 clear · partial: Edge cases, Words with no number") that a busy PM must wade through.
evidence.respects_words: Keeps Invoices untouched and refuses to invent a push remote, but the default reads "every heading everywhere" narrowly (keeps stat captions) and Done means lists only Settings for descriptions.
evidence.overall: Strong intake: finds the real blocker (no git repo), surfaces the ambiguity in note 1 with a sensible default, and asks little; dragged down slightly by the noisy brief and a narrow reading of "everywhere".
